newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares slide on late dollar sale.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares slide on late dollar sale.

text.p: The Mexican peso regained some ground lost earlier against the dollar at the close of trade on Friday after a big player sold a long dollar position, traders said.
"A large bank was long dollars after buying for corporate clients," a trader said. "They waited until the last minute before selling."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.5 and 1.1 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9130/7.9180 and 7.9090/7.9120 per dollar.
Traders said the peso also moderated its earlier slide when dealers sold surplus dollars they had bought in early trade.
Dollars were in demand from the opening bell in response to an early surge in U.S. long bond rates that followed publication of strong U.S. sales and producer prices data.
"The dollar was in some demand, but due to speculation by banks because of the way other markets opened," another trader said, referring to the U.S. stock and bond markets and the Mexican bourse.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 23/32 to yield 7.17 percent, while the Dow Jones was down 133.48 points at 6,406.57.
The Mexican bourse's blue chip IPC index was down 1.56 percent at 3,762.09.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.4 centavos weaker at 7.9240/7.9280 per dollar.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9000/7.9500 for the 48-hour peso next week.
